- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast lows, especially near horizon end.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply downward correction by 5–15% for next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early horizon (1–7 days) — if forecast is >10% above recent mean, adjust downward.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the shift; re-estimate from 10–15 days ahead with upward bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates late-period (last 10–15 days) — apply downward bias of 3–8% for final 10 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If official event (e.g., policy change, auction) occurs within 5 days, model often misses it — adjust forecast upward if event is bullish, downward if bearish.
